What was equally pleasing for Jim in winning this his first Championship was beating fellow clubmate Simon Holmes, who with David Harvey was running in this one as a guest.
Backing up Simon were:- 40th, Dave Harvey (15m. 43s.); 66th, Len Hobbs (16m. 45s.); 67th Reg Hopkins (16m. 46s.); John Cambridge 84th in 18m. 09s.; and Tony Holmes, who clocked 20m. 34s.

David Harvey ran in the 600m and although not in the first four, his was a very worthwhile effort. His ambition is to break 2.00 for the 800mts this season, I have every reason to believe he will manage it if he continues the way he is going.
The above three have been selected for the All-England meeting, but Dave Harvey is still in with a chance of selection, following his third place in the intermediate 800m. in 2m. 3.2s.

Young Dave Harvey made good use of his 680 yards allowance to win fairly comfortably in 9m. 12s., a highly promising performance. Chris Keavey took second place, off 560 yards, while Guy Monnet raced through to third place, off 220.
In the youths' events, Dave Harvey and Simon Holmes had good middle-distance wins, and weren't afraid to try their hand at field events either.

Reg Hopkins was a double winner in the youths' events, taking the pentathlon and the high-jump, while in this section, we also won the long-jump, through Stephen Crosbie, the shot-putt, through Dave Raffell, and the 800m., through fast-improving Dave Harvey.
LEFT David Harvey, seen here showing his paces in a Surrey League fixture, went on to win the Surrey youths' 800m. in June, and took third place in the London Schools' intermediate 800m.

While the seniors were disporting themselves over 5-miles, a small youths team, led by Simon Holmes and David Harvey were tackling a 3-mile course, and although the result below shows that they took fourth place, it can be seen that they were not so far out of snatching second.
